pageCache.text:
Vision & Ethos
At Thames View Infants we strive to provide a caring, fun and supportive learning environment, in which every child and their family, really do matter.
Mission Statement
We strive to orchestrate a fully ‘joined up’ provision, where all children, regardless of their starting point, reach their full potential. We say we help “every child and their family achieve their best”, which reflects our highly inclusive, well-supported and personalised provision.
We teach children to respect, accept and value their classmates and adults in our richly diverse multicultural school community and in their lives outside School by being role models.
We want children to enjoy their time at School and we endeavour to create a comfortable and secure environment in which they feel cared for and valued by developing the children’s independence, confidence and ability to make decisions for themselves.
We say that we are a “School of Leaders” and aim to empower children to make choices, be heard and negotiate through life by giving talk4learning a high profile.
The teaching of reading and writing is at the heart of what we do; and with a rich-ICT curriculum, we work hard to equip children with essential skills for later life.
Children have only one chance in life. We pride ourselves on our vibrant, high-quality teaching and careful feedback – helping to give all children the best learning experience possible.
We aim to make our School Community a welcoming, friendly and safe environment. We believe that it is important that parents and teachers work alongside each other, with “parents as partners”, to help and support children to thrive. We say that TVI places itself “at the Heart of the Community”. We pride ourselves on our offer of bespoke family support and parenting advice.
Communication is key. We value our open-door ethos and work hard to instil trust and transparency within families. Changing long-standing traditional dispositions to learning is a long-standing ambition of ours. Together, with your trust and support, we are making a real difference to our children’s lives and their futures.
Our very vibrant and carefully tailored curriculum, is rich and broad, with a high emphasis on precise teaching, first-hand experiences, talk4learning, enrichment, and developing play and social skills. There’s an enhanced SLCN provision and care has been taken to offer any additional support required within a “parallel learning model”. This maintains the School’s commitment to inclusivity and a full curriculum for all, including ensuring equitability for the lowest attaining 20%.
This is achieved by:
TVI is a Professional Learning Community and staff at different levels support Schools locally and beyond. This reputation is embedded within a portfolio of awards and articles. We’re particularly proud of our ability to grow new staff, particularly the less experienced, valuing their strengths and recognising their potential contribution to the greater School Community.
overcome anti-institutional perceptions
challenge traditionally-held dispositions to learning

Our Vision for Learning
Thames View Infants is a unique place to learn. Our children thrive. Our learning culture prepares children exceptionally well for the next stage in their life-long journey. The documents on this page help to capture the essence of this unique “sparkle” and our special vision for learning.
Signature Pedagogy
Parents ask us about how we organise and structure learning and lessons with the School day. We have a distinct learning ethos and the below documentation helps describe this “signature pedagogy”.
Our Signature Pedagogy Described
Features of a Nursery classroom at TVI
Features of a Reception classroom at TVI
Features of a KS1 classroom at TVI
Curriculum Sequencing
Our curriculum is carefully planned and particularly well sequenced. Knowledge and skills are introduced, consolidated and then revisited, ensuring learning deepens over time. In the spirit of Bruner’s Spiral Curriculum, children move from first-hand, practical and concrete experiences, to progressively more abstract learning, as skills are applied and mastery is deepened. This is embedded within and across subjects. Our curriculum has it’s foundations within the Early Years’ Framework and the National Curriculum Programmes of Study, sculpted by the School’s Leadership Team. It aspires to prepare children exceptionally well for the next stage of their development and education; including a successful transition into the Year 3 curriculum at Thames View Juniors. It gives children the best educational start, equipping them with the skills and attributes for later life, aspiring for them to access the full range of higher and further educational establishments. Our curriculum has evolved over time, with leaders adapting and modifying in response to the changing needs of the children, statutory requirements and their own expertise.

Partnerships
We have a number of partnerships with local schools and businesses.
The Collaborative Partnership of Thames View Infant and Junior Schools
Thames View Infants and Thames View Juniors have worked together in a Collaborative Partnership for a number of years. Doing so has benefited our children and families tremendously over time. Both Schools have retained their own individual identities, but by having a close working relationship, we have improved transitions between Year 2 (TVI) and 3 (TVJ) and have become more ‘joined up’ in our thinking. Teachers, Leaders and Directors from Thames View Infants and Juniors work together closely so that all children passing through both schools benefit from a more equitable provision and have even more chances to succeed.
Sharing Resources
Improving learning across both settings
Pooling expertise
Running shared clubs for all pupils
Greater consistency
Work placements, Work experience and more!
We work closely with a number of local Schools, Colleges and Universities, which we have nurtured over the years. We support students and trainees who are at different stages in their own learning journeys. We also host and lead events for partner professionals too, showcasing the work that we do.

After-School Clubs
TVI runs an extensive After School Provision
TVI runs an extensive After School Provision
Families at both Infant and Junior Schools can book an extended after-School Care Provision until 6pm each term-time evening, run by independently by Premier Education. Premier are Ofsted registered. Their offer includes a cooked meal and a range of activities. (Junior School families should select “Years 3-6” from the booking page. A member of Premier Education’s team will escort children safely to the Infant School until the end of your session). If this provision suits your needs, here is more information about their offer.
The Government’s Tax-Free Child Care Scheme offers eligible working families up to £500 every 3 months (up to £2,000 a year) for each child attending this or other approved childcare schemes. This rises up to £1,000 every 3 months if a child is disabled (up to £4,000 a year).
There are a number of regulated child-minders local to our School who offer alternative wrap-around care services. If these suit you more, please contact the School Office for details.
School Staff run Enrichment Learning Sessions until 4pm. These sessions cover a range of curricular subjects and run usually across a term. Families apply from a list of subjects available on the ParentMail App. We try our best to match children with their first or second preferences, but due to the high demand, this is not always possible.
We also run Additional After School Lessons until 4pm, for specific children who we feel would benefit from this additional provision. We normally contact individual Parents/Carers directly about this offer, as places are limited and we find it does not always suit all children. If you feel that your child needs extra help with their learning, please contact your child’s Class Teacher in the first instance.

Breakfast Club
We offer a Breakfast Club!
We offer a Breakfast Club!
Our Breakfast Club offer runs from 8am each School Day. It is run by School Staff for children in Reception or KS1.
We prioritise places for working families, those studying or where there is a need. Children arrive between 8am-8:20am.
Families book places via the ParentMail App. Families can block-book or choose days on an ad-hoc basis.
For all enquiries, please contact the School Office

Directors also stand on the Finance, Premises & Personnel Committee, which meet 6 times a year and has delegated responsibility for all staffing, personnel, health & safety, finance and budgetary matters.

Members of The Academy Trust
Academy Trusts are founded by Members who have a general duty to exercise their powers, to further the academy trust’s charitable purpose. They sit at “the top of the tree” in terms of a Trust’s Governance structure. Members help to ensure that Academy Trustees (Directors) are exercising effective governance by utilising a range of powers including: appointing and removing any or all serving Academy Trustees. The following professionals are Members of the Academy Trust:
Linda Trapnell
Leonie Malvo

Local Advisory Board (LAB) at Thames View Infants
The LAB sits “underneath” the Board of Directors and is made up of Staff, Parents and valued Members of the Community. The LAB at Thames View Infants meet each term and assists the Trust Board by being responsible for ensuring that the quality of learning remains high at Thames View Infants, and that the children achieve well and make sustained and substantial progress across the School. The LAB is responsible for all curriculum-related improvement, pupil matters and reviews certain School Policies. They also ensure that children thrive within a safe and nurturing environment.
Any Parent with a child in the school is eligible to stand for election as a LAB member and Parents will be notified when an election is due to take place. LAB members attend regular learning walks across School and are invited to attend courses which aim to help them fulfil their responsibility.

Prospectus
Click below for a Summary of our prospectus, translated into our most commonly-spoken home languages.
Thames View Infants is a bright and welcoming School, originally built in 1953. It serves the most deprived ward within the 6th most deprived Local Authority nationally.
Between 2008-2012, (with help from the London Thames Gateway Development Corporation), the School grew in size and now encompasses 12 classrooms, a nursery, 2 halls and offices. It provides a lively, cheerful environment for children and staff.
Achievement at TVI is well above the national average. End of KS1 Attainment has been ranked the highest of all schools within LBBD since 2009 and – more recently – within the top 3% of all Schools nationally (at Expected+ and within the top 1% of all Schools at Greater Depth).
The nursery is situated opposite the school in a large annex shared with the Chestnuts Nursery, which includes a separate play area.
The school is fully accessible with ramps located at all entrances to offer wheel chair access. There are additional classrooms in the playground, which provide the school with accommodation for a range of group activities. An extensive variety of after school clubs take place in the school.
Thames View Infants is a national trail blazer and staff often contribute to conferences and events both regionally and nationally. We have won a variety of awards and are invited to contribute to local news radio. We regularly share expertise on driving attainment, standards in Learning, Attainment, ICT, Supporting Families, Leadership and Community Cohesion.
Cited in a Governmental White Paper for valuing “Parents as Partners”, TVI continues to strive to offer the best possible learning experience for all pupils and adults alike; winning the e-Learning Foundation’s “Best Primary of the Year Award” in 2012 and receiving a special commendation in the 2013 Pupil Premium Awards. Headteacher Paul Jordan, (in post since 2007), was the only London-shortlisted Headteacher in the 2017 TES Headteacher of the Year awards. Our third successive Outstanding Ofsted Inspection during 2024, placed TVI in a very prestigious and unique position within our Local Authority’s Family of School’s.
Committed to working closely with partners and schools locally within LBBD and across London, Thames View Infants became an Academy in 2012 and in 2017 gained Multi Academy Trust Status (a part of TVI Learning). Since 2014, Thames View Infants has supported other Schools as a National Leader of Education (NLE). With well-established partnerships with UEL and Teach Redbridge, TVI continues to support Initial Teacher Training (ITT). Our Trust, TVI Learning, is currently working with the DfE to build a brand new local Primary School, called Fords View Primary to open soon on the Beam Park Development Park.
